newsitem.title: SPAIN: ATHLETICS-KIPRONO BIDS FOR WORLD HALF MARATHON TITLE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KIPRONO BIDS FOR WORLD HALF MARATHON TITLE.

text.p: Josphat Kiprono is aiming to become the third Kenyan in five years to lift the individual men's world half marathon title when he competes here on Sunday.
His compatriots Benson Masya and Moses Tanui won in 1992 and 1995 respectively.
Kiprono is the second fastest runner ever over the 21.097 kms distance with a time of 59 minutes 46 seconds, clocked in Milan in March this year.
He is the fastest man in the 165-strong field by a long way although he has a modest international record and missed out on selection for Atlanta.
Kiprono captains a Kenyan squad which has won the men's team title in four previous editions of the championship.
Last year Kenya filled the first three places in the men's race and although Tanui is not defending his title, the 1995 bronze medalist Charles Tangus will also be on the starting line.
The men's race looks set to be dominated by African runners with strong Tanzanian, Ethiopian and South African squads competing.

By contrast Europeans should lead the women's race. Britain's Liz McColgan holds the accepted world best time for the distance of 67 minutes 11 seconds, set in Tokyo four years ago, and starts as favourite.
McColgan had a disappointing Olympics, finishing only 16th in the marathon, but rallied to win the Great North Run, a British half marathon race from Newcastle to South Shields, earlier this month.
The Scottish runner won the inaugural women's title in 1992 but will have to work hard if she is to finish ahead of Romania's Christina Pomacu and Anuta Catuna, who were second and third last year.
South Africa's Zola Budd Pieterse is also in the women's field, but now aged 30 the former teenage prodigy is far from her old form.
